Now as for the work that I did, the work was the same before the war and during the war and our duties boiled down to the following: To maintaining law and order, fighting crime, offering security and safety and assistance to other organizations and institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And is the civilian police to be distinguished from any organisation referred to as the military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the military structures, I'm not aware of them. I don't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. know about that. But I do know that before the war as well, if there wasn't any military police, then we as civilian police men would be able to take somebody into custody if they were disturbing the peace or engaged in a crime. But we had to inform the nearest military unit straight away, of the military police, for them to take further steps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, on July 1st, 1992, did you attend a meeting of the Srebrenica War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 1st of July, 1992, I was present and that's when I was appointed and promoted as chief of the service for public security of the Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber who was also present at the meeting on July 1st?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: At that same meeting all the previous people were present from the 20th of May and there were quite a number of them because it was an expanded meeting where members of the War Presidency were elected, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Where did the meeting for the War Presidency, on July 1st, take place? In what location? What city, town, village?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: That was -- the first meeting on the 25th of May was in Bajramovici, and the second was a little further away from Bajramovici. There's a settlement called Stupina, a village called Stupina between Bajramovici and Srebrenica. Stupina was the name, Sab Bojna [phoen] Stupina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Pardon me. Is that where the meeting on July 1st took place, in Stupina?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: At Stupina, yes, on the 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And is that in the Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And you said that people who were present at that meeting had been present at the meeting of May 20th. Does that mean that Naser Oric was present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were appointments made at that first meeting or that meeting of the War Presidency similar to appointments that were made on the 20th of May?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were. They were. But the president of the War Presidency was elected, or rather municipality president, and at the same time he performed the duty of president of the War Presidency. So it would appear actually that the civilian authorities were established then too, headed by the president of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Please give the name --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: That's how it turned up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Pardon me. Please give the name of the president of the municipality that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, the president of the municipality, Mr. Hajrudin Avdic, was put forward, nominated, and elected.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness and the Trial Chamber to look at the screen, at a photo.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes. Oh, it's gone away. This gentleman is Hajrudin Avdic, on the screen, 28.11.92, or whatever other numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment now. Keep the freeze as this. Which document is this taken from Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a video that is P -- one moment, please. I'm sorry. We have to ask for a number for this document. What it is is there are two videos that are extremely similar that the Trial Chamber has already seen, but this is video number 5315.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But does it have an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. I would ask for one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's an identical copy of 393, which does have a P number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, the witness was shown just one slide from a video that Ms. Sellers has referred to and precisely the slide which is clocked at 03.59.1. It carries the date of the 28th of November of 1992, at time shown being 14 hours, 11 minutes. And the words and the text, interpreter, are these foreign? And they have "/unclear/full stop."

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to say we're not entering it for the text underneath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is just to identify the...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So that's Hajrudin Avdic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I would like to submit that into evidence. I would like to also inform the Trial Chamber that the similar video has P number 318.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what number -- what number should we give this video, Registrar, please? 51 -- 517. So this video, which contains this shot here, will be given Prosecution Exhibit P517.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Bogilovic, at the meeting that took place on the 1st of July, you stated that you were appointed to a position of public security station. Were there any appointments that were given to persons such as Hamdija Fejzic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I think there were, because that's when the civilian protection was formed. Jusuf started working before that, but that's when it came to be known as the civilian protection because it had to deal with the infrastructure in town, clean up the infrastructure and set that in order. So, Nurija Jusofovic was appointed commander of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is that Nurija Jusofovic who you testified earlier was your deputy?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same man, surname and first name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did a person named Jusuf Halilovic receive an appointment as well?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Jusuf Halilovic was appointed the leader of civilian protection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to have the witness shown the original of P42 and I believe that the English will be in Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at the document that is in front of you and confirm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Usher, could we have the English version put on the ELMO, please. It's for, the public won't be able to follow the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, if you look at the document before you, would you confirm that it accurately reflects what you have testified about in terms of the person or the meeting of the War Presidency on the 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as this text is concerned, it was written in pencil and Hamdija wrote it down into a notebook. These names, yes, they were those, and as to this piece of paper, well, I'm looking at it for the first time because we didn't have this format at the time, nor did we have the typewriter or anything like that. Yes, Hamdija and Fejzic president of the executive board. Now with Resid Effendic, there was a problem there that he was secretary. He never actually worked in that post because he was ill and couldn't come to work. Oric Naser, yes. Becir -- yes -- Bogilovic, that was the policeman. Halilovic, yes. Dudic, Mandic, Sefik, Mekic, Asiz [phoen], and Tabahric. Yes, yes, eleven members there. Those were the ones. And this was to be expanded in time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, due to your appointment, under article 10 as the chief of public security, who became your direct superior or your boss?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: My immediate superior was the president of the War Presidency, or rather, president of the municipality, Avdic Hajrudin, and I was duty-bound to report to him, both orally and in writing, and to follow his orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you look at the bottom of the document, where there is a signature on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Had you had occasions to see the signature of the person you've described as your boss, Hajrudin Avdic, on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I did have occasion to see his signature, when he called me to attend meetings, or rather, the first document appointing me was on the 14th of October, 1992 and that's when I saw it. So the first document in this format I received on the 14th of October, 1992, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature on the right-hand side of this document as that of your former boss, Hajrudin Avdic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he just scrawled something down. Probably it is. Most probably. That's what his scrawl looked like.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We can remove the document from the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, on July 1st, 1992, to your knowledge was anyone appointed or asked to perform the task of chief of military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As for that, the appointment of chief of military police, I don't know about that. I know that on the 1st of July there was somebody appointed komandir of the military police. As to the chief on the 1st of July, nobody was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Would you please tell the Trial Chamber who was appointed komandir of the military police.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As commander of the military police on the 1st of July, Mirzet Halilovic was elected, nickname Mirza.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you know Mirzet Halilovic prior to July 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I knew Mirzet just slightly. Well, he went to secondary school. I don't know where he graduated. Maybe from Bratunac. I didn't know him well. I got to know him during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was he a former police officer, or was he a police officer prior to the war?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Before the war there was some sort of teams that went to Zagreb, to the police there. They would go and come back. I really don't know whether he went or not. Probably he went somewhere, he was sent somewhere, but I can't confirm that because I don't know for certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When Mr. Mirzet Halilovic was appointed to be commander of the military police, how did his function differ from your function now as chief of public security or that of Nurija Jusofovic who was, you said, your successor for the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As far as the functions were concerned, where Jusofovic Nurija and the civilian police, he was called the komandir and so was the other person, he was known as the komandir of the military police. Now what the authority and competences of the civilian police was, I know about that; as to the military police, I really don't know. I'm not a soldier so I know nothing about the army and can't tell you about the military police. As far as my function is concerned, mine was higher.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show the witness the original document P109, and I believe that the English will be put on our Sanctions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I ask you to look at the document, and if you would go to the third paragraph down, does that reflect your testimony in terms of the appointment of Mr. Mirzet Halilovic as commander of the military police unit?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As I said a moment ago, this is how it stood. The decision was made to form the wartime military police, that's what I said, and Mirzet Halilovic was appointed the commander of the unit, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you look at the second paragraph of this document. Does it also accurately reflect what occurred, in terms of appointments, at the meeting of the War Presidency on the 1st of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because he was elected on the 1st, just like everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And are you aware of an appointment of Hamid Alic to any position or post?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Hamid?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw that question. Mr. Bogilovic, you don't have to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Hamid is not there. There's Hamed, with an E. Yes. Hamed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Hamed came to Srebrenica at that time. He told us about the situation. He was communications man. He worked at the post office in Bratunac, so he was taken away to be executed by a firing squad and he survived, and he came back and together with another man, who was also a communications person, who was familiar with communications, they were both appointed to this communications position.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will reinstate the question, if possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would then again ask you, at the bottom right-hand corner, would you look at the signature and does that resemble the signature of the person that we've referred to as Naser Oric who was present at the War Presidency meeting on July 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I have to apologise once again. This is the first time that I see this piece of paper. So the same situation again as regards the signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You can remove the document from the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, on the 2nd July, 1992, were you injured in any form or way?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: On the 2nd of July, that is the Muslim New Year.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the microphone be turned on for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The shelling began and the dead started coming in, the couriers informed us, and of course we went to check what was happening in that part of the area. A trench that was in our terrain in the village of Likari, the house that was attacked by the Serb forces, a father and a son were taken away and they disappeared without a trace. This is where they set up their artillery, and this is where they fired from. We went -- I and Elvir, a police officer of mine, we went there to see how we could help, and because we had a small truck we had to leave it in Potocari and we went there. We encountered several of our soldiers, shells were falling down, and when the shell would fall, we would run there, wait for the next one to fall, and then we went to a trench, because about 30 of our lads were there. We wanted to get them out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, were you injured as a result of the shelling on that day on July 2nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As we approached that area, as I was going to check another trench to check whether anybody was there, I was wounded. There was a Serb section there and somebody there fired from his rifle at me and I was wounded. A man, a young man was walking behind me and he asked me whether I was wounded, and I said yes, and then he covered me with his fire as I crawled back. They took me to a house in Srebrenica. There were no windows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You did not receive good training when you were studying to become a policeman. Please, try to answer the question and just the question and nothing beyond that. You were just asked a simple question. You gave us a whole story. You were asked whether you were injured on the 2nd of July. No one asked you how, where and by whom. You just -- you were just asked a simple question. And you have given us the answer. So next question, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: As a result -- thank you, Your Honour. As a result of your injury, were you -- did you go to a hospital for a period of two weeks followed by a period of convalescence for two months?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: After I was wounded, I was taken to a hospital. It was not a hospital proper, it was just a house. A doctor by the name of Dzanic was in that house. Since it turned out that the conditions there were not proper, there were no window panes, lice appeared, infestation by lice, a colleague came for me and took me to his house. I had to sign --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Bogilovic. Might I please ask the next question. Was the colleague whose house you went to Mr. Zulkic? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. One moment because we still haven't got the answer to the previous question, whether he stayed first sort of under treatment for two weeks, followed by a period of convalescence of two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes or no, Mr. Bogilovic, is that a fair assessment of the extent of your period of convalescence?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is it true that during this time period, that you were unable to go to work on a daily basis but that you did try and maintain contact with Nurija Jusofovic who was your deputy and now was appointed chief of the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: During the time period of your convalescence, did Akif Ustic visit you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Akif Ustic did visit me when I was in the hospital. Because that -- his house was close to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now ask you to look at the monitor at a photograph. This is now called P17 -- I'm sorry, P517. Would you tell the Trial Chamber if you recognise the person in blue in that photo.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Oric and Mr. Ustic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is that the Mr. Ustic who you referred to in terms of his appointment to the Srebrenica Municipal Staff and the person who visited you when you were convalescing?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. For the record, the clip that the witness is being referred to and which is on Sanction at moment is clocked -- is taken from Exhibit P517?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And is clocked at 02 hours 35 minutes 8 seconds. It shows the date of August 1992 - 8th, 1992 - and has the time 16 hours eleven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that that is in minutes and not hours. It would be 2 minutes, 35 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Two minutes, 35 seconds, and 8 milliseconds also. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, you may remove the picture from the Sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, did Naser Oric also visit you during this time period of your convalescence?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he visited me once in town in this house and he did visit me once in the house where I was staying with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now during the period in which you had to nurse your injury, did the offices of the civilian police move out of the new territorial building, territorial defence building?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: When I was wounded, they were still in the staff building and Nurija then moved to the old police station building while I was away.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now when you say the "old police station building," is that the building where you worked when you were a police officer in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: That is the building where I worked for 20 years.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Is that building also referred to as the SUP or the MUP?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it had several names SUP, MUP because it used to be the secretariat then it became the ministry, but it's the same thing, SUP or MUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And could you please explain to the Trial Chamber, where was the military police located during this time period? Now we're speaking about August or September 1992. Where were their offices located?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Their offices were on the ground floor and our offices were on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Does that mean the offices of the military police were on the first floor, the SUP or MUP, and the offices of the civilian -- I'm sorry were on the ground floor, and the offices of the civilian police were on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned -- you said the civilian and civilian. The military police was on the ground floor and the civilian police was upstairs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like you to now look at a photo that is on Sanctions. Mr. Bogilovic, can you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, I want to make sure that he is on Sanction. He is on Sanction? All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: This is P446, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The witness is being shown a clip from P446, clocked at 1 minute 14 seconds.2.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, looking at this photograph, can you tell me what it is a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This photograph depicts the entrance, and to the right of the entrance is the -- where the duty officer was, and this is also where the military police was. And here, upstairs, was the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, is this a photograph of the SUP or the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This is, as you say yourself, the SUP or MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: The part of the photograph that indicates gray brick on the ground level, which of the forces were located there; the military police or the civilian place?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: The military police was located on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And the part of the photograph that appears to have a white covering or facade, is that where the civilian police were located?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the civilian police was upstairs. Here, where the wall is white.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Now, is that where Mr. Halilovic worked, on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic was on the ground floor, that is where his police force was and his duty officer. Duty service.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: For the moment we can remove the photo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please try and tell the Trial Chamber, during the period of August, September or October, what, if you know, was the reputation of Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Had you ever heard any complaints or any things that were favourably said about Mr. Halilovic, in terms of his function as komandir of the military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I could not really meddle in that, because the tasks were divided between the civilian and the military police. At any rate, I was unable to work at that time, so I couldn't do anything. I had problems with my leg. I had sepsis two times.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever, in September, October, November visit the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did go there. On the 14th of October, I was invited by the president to come and attend a meeting. I attended this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever oversee or come and see what the work of Nurija Jusofovic was at the SUP building during the time period of August, September, or October?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. From time to time, whenever I was able to do so, when somebody would drive me there. But on most occasions Nurija would come and see me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: What was the relationship between Nurija Jusofovic and Mr. Halilovic in terms of their professional relationship? How -- and Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. also how well did they great along as professionals?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that they went along all that well, because there was a little bit of arrogance on the part of Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Had you, as chief of public security or as a member of the War Presidency, ever received or heard complaints about how Mr. Halilovic carried out his function?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I did receive complaints from the citizens that he was acting arrogant, that he would carry out searches and would not issue receipts, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: As a former police officer of 20 years, did you think that that was improper behavior or conduct for a police officer, whether military or civilian?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this was not proper for anyone, an ordinary citizen and let alone a police officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Mr. Halilovic during that time period, about the complaints that you received?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: If I tried to talk to him, he would refuse, because he really was an arrogant person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, when you went to the MUP or SUP building in the month of September or October, did you ever see Serb prisoners on the ground floor of the building?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: No. No, no. I would get in and I would pass through. I did not go there very often, but I would always go straight upstairs, precisely because of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And when you say "him," are you referring to Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I mean Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did the civilian police detain Serb prisoners during the month of September, October in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: The civilian police, no, no. The civilian police could not do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So, is it your testimony the civilian police did not detain Serb prisoners throughout the war or particularly between 19 -- April 1992 until March 1993 in Srebrenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: As for the civilian police, they certainly did not arrest Serbs or detain them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would briefly like to show a video clip of the inside of the SUP building. We have seen it before but I would just like to point out a couple of things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, P -- it is P46.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Halilovic, if you look at the image in front of you, would you please tell me, do you recognise this image?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: That's the staircase taking you upstairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the moment, for the record, the clip that the witness is referring to is the one which is clocked at 3 minutes, 22 seconds, point 8. This is from Exhibit P46.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: P446, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, if one were to go up to those stairs, would they then come to the offices of the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They would go up and then it comes back.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We're going to continue for just a couple of seconds.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, do you see, on the left-hand side of this image, a door and then you see what appears to be light or a door. Could you tell the Trial Chamber, if you know, where that door leads. On the right-hand side. I'm very sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: On the left. To my left. Probably you mean this. There's a window over there. And this first door is the detention room, looking at it from this angle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So one moment. Stop, stop, stop. For the record, the witness was being referred to a clip at 3 minutes, 41 seconds, point 6 or 7. And he has indicated the -- what appears to be a door at the extreme right of the clip as being the entrance to the detention room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I have the arrow placer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. The arrow, while you had said left, the arrow was indicating right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the witness was referring to the right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, could you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you see that arrow, Mr. Bogilovic? Can you see a small --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that the entrance to the detention room that you referred to -- referred us to before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That's where the duty officer was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's go the opposite direction now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's the detention room there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So for the record, the door which is being indicated by the witness as being the entrance to the detention room, is the first one on the left-hand side of the scene or the photo, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: We'll continue just a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you please look at this image in front of you now. Is this how the -- is this -- would you please tell the Trial Chamber what this image is.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: These look like bars. I'm not quite clear what that is, bars, because I know that there were -- there was a door to that particular room.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing that this can be, could be a photograph from the basement where there were some logs, wood was kept there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, the witness is referring to clip clocked at 3 minutes, 58 seconds, point 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, when you worked at the police station, during your 20 years as a police officer, do you recognize or remember that room in the police station?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I remember it well. There was a door. It had a door at the entrance, and some appellate like a bed where they could lie down, and it had bars on the window, so I'm not quite clear on what these bars are here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were those bars present when you retired in 1991 from the Srebrenica police force on -- in that room?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: When I went, they weren't there. The bars weren't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Did you use this room when you were a police officer as a holding cell, a detention cell, or a place to keep people who were arrested?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We did use the room for detaining people, for detention. A holding cell. From different periods: For six hours, 12 hours, or 24 hours, depending on the offence that the person had committed, whether the person was under the influence of alcohol, whether they were drunk or not. Unless the court determined other detention periods.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And Mr. Bogilovic, when you detained persons in your 20 years as a police officer, how would you secure them in that room so that they could not leave on their own free will?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: We would lock the door. There was a key and you would lock the door. And if they were making any disturbances, shouting or making any noise, you would have to tie them. If they were under the effects of alcohol, then you would have to bring in a doctor to see that they hadn't -- they weren't suffering from alcohol poisoning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. We will continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, do you recognise this room in the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This is probably the toilet, the WC.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Was there a bathroom there when you worked there during the 20-year period? Was there a bathroom in that room? I mean a toilet in that room?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Not a bathroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I mean a toilet in that bathroom.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: A toilet, yes, there was a WC. Without a toilet seat. It was just the type where you crouch down.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, do you recognize these scenes in the building?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This is the door on the left-hand side as you enter the police station, the entrance door. And that is where the administration was for registration of your car, for your ID cards, for your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop. Stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The treasury office, and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take me back a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, stop. Stop. The witness was being shown the clip which is clocked at 4 minutes and 58 seconds point 3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you recognise --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, did Mirzet Halilovic have his offices on the first floor in any of the rooms that we have seen on the video clip?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think he had any special office. There was the duty office. Had he had a separate office or cabinet, no, I don't think he did. At least, I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did he work on that first floor, on that ground floor of the SUP building?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to decide whether it is the first or the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The previous question referred to the first floor. So I want to make sure that his answer is related to the first floor and not to the ground floor. Did Mr. Halilovic have an office in that building; and if he did, on which floor was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The offices were of the military police, they were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Well, the witness said first floor and then he said ground floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ground floor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It all belonged to them. Then up on the story above was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So can you tell us if Mr. Halilovic had an office at ground floor level?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Personally, his own personal office, you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know that he had a special separate personal office. I really don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he was based on the ground floor of that building, not on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what you mean by ground floor and first floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I put the image back on the system.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the top part, it's the ground floor. Are you on this here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think if you show me exactly. Where would Mr. Halilovic be, in the gray part or in the painted part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the entrance. That's the entrance. [Indicating] Just there where you show it. So to the right, the window on the right, that was the duty officer's office, where Halilovic and his duty police worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think that is enough. Let's move.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record -- no, can I have that picture again, please, sorry. For the record, the clip that the witness was referring to is one clocked at 1 minute, 14 seconds, point 3. And he indicated the -- what appears to be the entrance to the building and to the window which, as you look at the screen, is at the right-hand side of the -- of that entrance.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, did there come a time period when Mr. Halilovic was placed under your authority or under your supervision, in September or October of 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of October, 1992, the president of the municipality called me to attend a meeting. I went to the meeting and the meeting took place in the cultural centre. And then I received a decision, in written form, A4 format, saying that Mirzet Halilovic came under my command.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Could you tell the Trial Chamber why Mirzet Halilovic would come under your command? What were the circumstances that prompted such a decision?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: The main reason is something that the president should know, the president who gave me the duty, because in the decision that I received it says that it came into force immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably in order to control -- better control them, because we -- we were in the same building.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you say "better control them," are you referring to the military police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Him. To him more.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I meant him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You're referring to Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Were you aware of Mr. Halilovic's reputation then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you put that question already.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I was trying to get more specific information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Initially he told you that he didn't, but then in an oblique manner he confirmed that he received various reports. Do you want to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I want to ask one more specific question concerning this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, were you aware whether Mr. Halilovic was to have been responsible for death or injury to Serb prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's make this clear. Basically, in other words, this Mr. Halilovic moved from under military command to under civilian command. And for all intents and purposes this was a demotion for him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is correct. It was a demotion. He was arrogant and didn't accept that, but when I received my assignments, I called him and talked to him, but he refused it. He turned a deaf ear and started doing things the way he thought they ought to be done. And that wasn't something that I could take, so I took a piece of paper and wrote down three or four -- I'm sorry, I don't have that -- I wrote three or four pages full to my superior, that is to say the president, and the president forwarded it on to the commander. And then Mirzet was replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, the witness didn't say before that Mr. Halilovic was under military command. He was placed under him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But if he is the komandir of the military police --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't make any assumption of any nature of that in the situation at the time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think you are right, Mr. Jones. Let me ask the question. When Mr. Halilovic was komandir of the military police, who was he answerable to? Who was he answerable to? Who was his immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, to the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, you have mentioned a meeting that took place on October 14th that you were asked to attend. Was that a meeting of the War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Who else was in attendance at that meeting, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by everyone; the army and us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you know the reason that the meeting was called?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. All I do know is that the president told me that there would be a meeting. Now, all the others, with their own departments, they had a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: At that meeting, did they discuss the military and the civilian police and discuss questions related to those two entities?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the main topic of discussion was that the situation ought to be settled, that is to say that the situation should be improved and the organisation should be better, where that was warranted and needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: When you say "situation," are you referring to the military police or the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Both. Because the civilians and the army, there were a lot of people coming in. There was a shortage of food. Many problems to contend with. And all of this led to a disruption of law and order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would ask that the witness be shown -- excuse me, Your Honour. Your Honour, we'll be looking at P84. And I would ask, in the English translation, I'm going to be referring to pages 7 through 10. I'll be looking at the section where it has an ERN number before the text, ERN 02115050. We might have the same problem of whether that concludes the text or begins it, but just so the people can find their place on page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Usher, please, if you could put page -- document 7 to Ms. Sellers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Starting with 7 and we will be going to page 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. Page 7, please on the ELMO. I can't translate the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, would you agree that on the agenda of that meeting was the organisation functioning in both the military and civilian authorities and what is referred to as the free territory?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I would like --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you encountering any difficulty in finding what you are being referred to, Mr. Bogilovic? Because if you need our help, we will try and help you as much as we can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like this section to be shown to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I -- I don't know. Unless someone gives me the text in the B/C/S version, which I don't have here... Let's put -- which page is he looking at? Does it finish at the top with 5050?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I have given him, I don't know whether you would like to have it, is the text that he looked at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. It's not there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He needs to be looking at 5050.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right? A few lines from the top in 5050, you see "agenda," and you are being asked to confirm that the agenda stated or indicated, as item 1: "Organisation and functioning of the military and civilian authorities in the free territory." Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He confirms that, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I would ask you to look at the following page, which would have ERN number -- I'm sorry, it would be at the bottom of 50, and you will see that there is a name that says Becir, and then there is -- appears to be a statement. In the English it comes after --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: What's the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It would still be on the page 50.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Begic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. There are a list of people and then there is a paragraph that begins: "Hierarchy. It discusses and assesses the war situation and takes decisions. It is both the supreme authority and the supreme command. Commanding takes places through the staff. It is directly the command of the military police --" there are some words crossed out -- "but at the same time military police is subordinated to the armed forces." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a proper --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me help him. Mr. Bogilovic, I heard you say a few seconds ago "Becir." It's the three or four lines above that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Three or so lines -- yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have an objection to the way that questions are phrased, because she is interpreting the text in -- she is giving the text an interpretation. I would now like to ask the witness to read the text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Becir, here where it says Becir, because -- well, this is not really very legible, that's the problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, the three or four lines before, do you see there, one after the other, commander, chief, deputy, assistant for security, assistant for POV, assistant for logistics, assistant for engineers? Do you see those words, that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Start reading immediately after that list, from the word "Hierarchy" until you reach to "Becir." Start reading, please. "Hierarchy."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it says hierarchy. But I can read some of the words, but some of the words I simply cannot read. For instance, the third word here, it says "assess" the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If he can't read it, he can't read it. We can do nothing about that. I'm not going to force the witness to try and guess what there is. Read it for yourself, to yourself first. And then tell us whether you can actually tell us what the substance of -- what it is or whether you would prefer to say: Sorry, I can't read it, I can't decipher the words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would prefer for somebody who is able to read it, to read it. Because I simply cannot. I see here that it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. says Becir and then it says "because." I probably mentioned a reason for something, and I would really like to know what it is that I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Forget "Becir." We are interested in the lines that are before Becir, not what Becir is reported as having said there. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be of assistance, perhaps the best thing would be to put this portion of the minutes on the ELMO. It is, in fact, quite clear and the interpreters can read it out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm grateful for the suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a very practical suggestion, Madam Vidovic, for which we are grateful. Let's put on the ELMO -- do you have it on Sanction as well? Or not? So if you have it on Sanction, we can see it on Sanction, just colour, highlight that paragraph and then zoom in on it, please. Mr. Bogilovic. Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Look at the monitor. Look at the monitor. Yes. Yes. You need to select from the second line, those four lines above "Becir." You see "hierarkija."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do. That is the first word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now try to read the rest, if you can. If you cannot, we will ask the interpreters to read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the interpreter to read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. There are so many, I don't know who will be shouldering the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters say that they cannot read it either and would somebody else like to have a go, if they know what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The only clever one that we have here is you, Madam Vidovic. Don't take it that I am asking you or that I am forcing you to read it. I mean, please don't --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I suggest, because if necessary, I mean, we have gone through this before with the CLS interpreter who read the text from this original to him, whether that could be an option. I certainly don't want to make Defence counsel to participate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be an extreme help, obviously. But obviously I want to make it clear that I am not asking you, but I would gladly accept if you did. So that's the position.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is an honour for me to be able to assist Mr. Bogilovic. I think that what it reads is the following: "Hierarchy. Analyses and assesses the war situation, makes decisions. It is the supreme authority and the supreme command. It exercises command through the staff. The immediate COM --" that is an abbreviation of the military police -- "but the VP, military police, is at the same time subordinate to the staff of the OS, the armed forces." Then it says: "Becir, because of the non-familiarity with the situation, the problems, we established the war staff, the War Presidency, and the operations staff. The decisions of any of these organs are not implemented. We have to establish a peoples' court. The armed forces, in fact, created disruptions or broke the law and order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam Vidovic, for your not only cooperation but valuable help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sellers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bogilovic, the name Becir, does that refer to you in these minutes?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Most probably, because I was the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: You mean the only Becir at the meeting of the War Presidency and the OS staff?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was the only Becir there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Do you recall responding in a like manner to the issue being raised as to the military police and whose command it came under?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Up until that time, it was under the military command. But the discussion was, at that time, that it should continue to be so. And what led to the situation in which I was in fact a commander to them, that they were in fact subordinate to me, it's a different matter. I really cannot give you an answer. Probably it was in order to be able to control them more easily and to be able to establish order. This meeting was in fact quite useful. And from that time on, the situation with the law and order and discipline was much better.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I would like to ask you to look further down on the document that would end in 51.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: It's on page 8 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What I suggest is that on the ELMO we have the English translation and on Sanction we stick to the B/C/S and any particular part that you refer the witness to, please we'll zoom in.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As much as we can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I am referring the witness to the part that begins with Nedred and concludes with a statement by Naser, but in the English version ends with the word "command."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the ELMO we need the middle of the page, Usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, are you able to read that part of the original document? Starting with Nedred, then the statements of what appears to be Mirza, and then Naser. Nedred.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It's Nedzad in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Pardon, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, rather than Nedred, it is actually Nedzad in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know, I can't read it myself. The top line, first line, first word is Nedzad or Nedred? Mr. Jones? If you look at Sanction, first line, first word, is it Nedred or Nedzad colon? No. Leave it where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: We have Nedzad in the B/C/S version which we have, and we understand that is what it is in the original.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says Nedzad here. The decisions are made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who would Nedzad be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nedzad Bektic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Bogilovic, are you able to read what Nedzad Bektic said?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I would like somebody else to read it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that somebody needs to read it for us to interpret.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only read "the decisions are made," and I cannot read what follows after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I have no solution. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will be pleased to be of assistance. "Decisions are made by the commander not by the staff." Then it says: "Mirza: The war staff should be expanded to include members of the operations staff. "Naser: All the current problems are caused by the organisation. All this boils down to the fact that everybody should do their own job, and later on, you can squabble about the government, the power. You should get smart. Let's make an organisation to fortify ourselves and to save ourselves. It is possible that there is ammunition in Fakovici and it hasn't been seized. If we want to be an army, we must know what the order is and we must have the commands." Should I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to place that other part now on Sanctions and which will be listing --

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Mr. Bogilovic first, does he remember that part of the discussion at the meeting of the 14th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I know that the purpose of this meeting was to resolve certain issues and to improve the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And after that discussion, did they try and put order in by naming the persons who were in charge of certain areas? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I think that the answer is, yes, that several people were appointed to different tasks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would just like for that next section to be placed on Sanctions. I believe that possibly Mr. Bogilovic will be able to recognize this, it is names and functions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, there appears to be a name here that says in the English translation "Osman." Could you please just, if you are able, to read that and then the list of names down to number 8.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I know Osman. He was the chief. I would like to ask somebody to read this and then I can comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I thank you for the last reading and I thank you in advance for this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Osman: Let's make things specific. Let's put names forward for various structures. Avdic - president (Hajrudin); president of the IO Executive Committee - Hamdija; secretary Ankic Esad; chief for economy remains the same; secretary of the secretariat for NO, National Defence, Hasanovic Suljo; chief of the CZ, civilian protection staff, Jusuf Halilovic; chief of the public security service, Becir (military police - Mirza; civilian police - Nurija); commander of the staff - Naser (not a member of the War Presidency); deputy - Zulfo -- deputy commander - Zulfo." And then one line below: "The staff of the armed forces --" shall I continue? Shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: No. Thank you very much. That is sufficient for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic, once more.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bogilovic, do you recall at that time period that it was discussed at the meeting --

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- both --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Finish your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: -- military police and civilian police were linked to the chief of public security, you, Becir.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: At this meeting, and that was on the 14th of October, the president told me, or rather, the president of the War Presidency that I would be superior to Mirzet, as I was to Nurija and all the others who were appointed. Some appointments were confirmed, others were added. And according to this, it was decided that the staff of the War Presidency was -- now, the question was who was superior to whom and who was subordinate to whom? We didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic. Would you just confirm that prior to the 14th of October, Mirzet Halilovic was not your subordinate.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't my subordinate, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... was he in the chain of command of the military prior to him being placed under you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Mirzet was appointed on the 1st of July 1992. And this is the 14th of October here that we're talking about, 14th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Would you just please answer my question, Mr. Bogilovic. Do you know whether he was in the military chain of command prior to being placed under you?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you. We can remove the document from the witness at this point. Mr. Bogilovic, did you write orders as the chief of public security?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I wrote orders to my police. I wrote orders about movements, the movement of citizens at that time, and so on and so forth, because of the shelling, so I issued orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And did you write orders pursuant to the legal authority that you were given to exercise your function as chief of public security?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: I think that was it, yes. As far as I was able to and on the basis of what I did before, I continued the work that I had done before, because if you felt the situation needed something to be done, if there was sources of shelling, then I would write posters saying that people shouldn't move around between such-and-such hours. This was confirmed later on when Mr. Morillon arrived with his elite. He provided an APC, because I went from the upper part to the lower part and used a megaphone, a loudspeaker.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness this last document before we conclude, Your Honours. This is P254. The witness is being shown the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Mr. Bogilovic, I would ask you to look at the document. And is this an order that you issued together with Hajrudin Avdic on the 14th of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This order, yes, it is. It's an order that was one of the subjects discussed at the meeting on the 14th of October, that law and order had been disrupted, and the decision was made at the time to go into action because, from the Zepa area, citizens were coming in, bringing in weapons and selling them for food. And then there were certain persons who were in possession of weapons without having permits. And all weapons had to be registered. So this was the decision that followed. This was what we had to do, to deal with the situation. So we issued orders that all those who had weapons and did not have permission to do so, were to hand over their weapons to the nearest unit and they would be issued a receipt in return for the weapons turned in.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And so therefore was the nearest unit, could that be a military unit or a civilian unit? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: At Zepa, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I'm asking you to -- referring you back to the order that you issued. And if you look on the first paragraph that comes under "We hereby order..." the last sentence, I'm asking you whether that could be to the nearest unit, be it military or civilian police. Mr. Bogilovic, is that what it says in the order that you issued?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: This order was issued because I, as of this date, was superior both to the military police, or rather, Mirza, so that this order was supposed -- Mirzet was supposed to act upon this order, as well as Nurija Jusofovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Just very briefly, that is your signature on the bottom left-hand side of the document?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is, and it is I who am issuing the order, or rather, the two of us. We are issuing orders that anyone in possession of a firearm must hand them over to the nearest units. Of course, a receipt would be issued, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: And that's Mr. Avdic's signature on the bottom right-hand side of the document?

utterances.speaker: BECIR BOGILOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. He signs first, because he's the top man, and then I sign second, but we both sign this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I could ask for the document to be taken from the witness, and today I will have no further questions and I must inform the Trial Chamber that we will have to continue with the witness on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I understand. I understand that. And given what you have just said and also what Madam Vidovic said in the beginning of the sitting, I look at Mr. Wubben and I suppose you will need to put your experience and wisdom and decide what the position will be like next week. Because, as I see it, there is no way we can finish with this witness on Monday. And if we don't finish with this witness on Monday, how much more -- how much longer do you think you will require, Ms. Sellers? Because I have tried to follow on the basis of the list of documents that you indicated, and we are past halfway, but...

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: I hoped to be much further than halfway. I think we might have to see if the Prosecution can arrange to have an interpreter with him to facilitate that. We're grateful for Defence counsel's assistance. And I will see if there is any manner in which we can possibly not go forward on some of the evidence that we would have called from this witness, but hopefully it would not be to the detriment of the Prosecution case. I do have to say that we are bound to present our case fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. You say you require five, six hours, that is basically two days, you know. You will get the five, six hours if you need them. This is an important witness. I'm not going to restrict --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour, I will need at least five hours. At least five or six hours. It's a fairly lengthy process. Because we have to make pauses for the interpretation, of course, and having heard the testimony of this witness so far, I don't think we will need less time, I think we will probably need more time. So I don't believe we will complete this -- well, in three days, yes, but I don't think we will get through an additional witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So, Mr. Wubben, I am going to leave this entirely to you and you will report back to the Trial Chamber on Monday. I'm sure that with your experience and your wisdom you will know exactly where you stand and whether you would need to have the next witness here in The Hague. Certainly I want to avoid a situation whereby we start the next witness and then send him home for a fortnight or so and then have him back. That is to be avoided at all costs. So I am going to leave it. You don't need to say anything now. I know I can put my trust in your hands and we will get good results afterwards. So having said that, Mr. Bogilovic, you've heard what has been just said. You will definitely be here Monday and Tuesday, if not also Wednesday. This is very tiring. I agree that this is tiring. So I kindly ask you to bear with us, because it is -- giving testimony is -- is no fun. We will try to be of assistance to you as much as we can. In the meantime, try to take advantage of the weekend and rest as much as you can, because you have a long journey ahead of you next week, this coming week when we start again on Monday. If at any time you feel tired, please do draw our attention and we will take that into consideration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we will reconvene Monday at 9.00 in the morning. Now, 9.00 in the morning I have another initial appearance -- 8.00 in the morning I have another initial appearance. From the looks of it, I should be able to finish it by 9.00, but it might take me an extra half hour. So we might start at half past nine on Monday rather than at nine. That's the position. All right. I will be starting at 8.00, so I will be worse off than the rest of you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of March, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.05 p.m.,
